note: Case studies shown on the Casebook site. Daily additions are appended here automatically.

items.title: Superblocks
items.designers: Ajuntament de Barcelona; Salvador Rueda / BCNecologia
items.scale: ≈ 400 × 400 m per superblock (3 × 3 blocks)
items.placement: Placed at the Sant Antoni superblock, one of several in the programme. Position from OpenStreetMap.
items.brief: Grouping nine Eixample blocks and pushing through-traffic to the perimeter turns interior streets into plazas, play space and shade.

items.title: The High Line
items.designers: James Corner Field Operations; Diller Scofidio + Renfro; Piet Oudolf
items.scale: 2.33 km elevated park
items.placement: Placed at the site. Position from OpenStreetMap.
items.brief: A disused freight viaduct on Manhattan's West Side planted as a linear park, with Oudolf's self-seeding planting design.

links.label: Friends of the High Line — History

items.title: Vauban
items.designers: City of Freiburg; Forum Vauban; Baugruppen co-housing groups
items.scale: ≈ 38 ha, ≈ 5,500 residents
items.placement: Placed at the site. Position from OpenStreetMap.
items.brief: A former barracks rebuilt as a car-reduced district of resident-led building groups, tram access and Passivhaus-standard homes.

items.title: Cheonggyecheon
items.designers: Seoul Metropolitan Government
items.scale: 10.9 km restored stream
items.placement: Placed at the site. Position from OpenStreetMap.
items.brief: An elevated expressway was torn down and the buried stream beneath it brought back as a sunken public promenade.

items.title: Metrocable
items.designers: Metro de Medellín; Municipality of Medellín (social urbanism)
items.scale: Line K ≈ 2 km, 4 stations
items.placement: Placed at Santo Domingo Savio, one station on the network. Position from OpenStreetMap.
items.brief: Cable-car lines linking hillside informal neighbourhoods to the metro, paired with library-parks and public works at each station.

items.title: The Sea Ranch
items.designers: Lawrence Halprin; MLTW (Moore Lyndon Turnbull Whitaker); Joseph Esherick
items.scale: ≈ 16 km of coastline
items.placement: Placed at the site. Position from OpenStreetMap.
items.brief: A coastal community planned from wind, hedgerows and meadows, with timber buildings clustered to leave the land open.

items.title: Aranya Housing
items.designers: Balkrishna Doshi; Vastu-Shilpa Foundation
items.scale: ≈ 85 ha, ≈ 6,500 dwellings
items.placement: Placed at the city centre, approximate. Position from OpenStreetMap.
items.brief: Sites-and-services housing with plinths, service cores and a street hierarchy, built so families could extend their homes over time.

items.title: Quinta Monroy
items.designers: Elemental (Alejandro Aravena)
items.scale: 93 families, ≈ 0.5 ha
items.placement: Placed at the site. Position from OpenStreetMap.
items.brief: "Half a good house": the state subsidy pays for the hard half, and families build the other half themselves inside the frame.

items.title: Byker Wall
items.designers: Ralph Erskine
items.scale: ≈ 620 homes in the Wall; ≈ 1,800 on the estate
items.placement: Placed at the site. Position from OpenStreetMap.
items.brief: A long, colourful perimeter block shelters a low-rise estate designed together with the residents, with an on-site architect's office.

items.title: Finger Plan
items.designers: Regional Planning Office (Peter Bredsdorff, Steen Eiler Rasmussen)
items.scale: Greater Copenhagen region
items.placement: Placed at the city centre, approximate. Position from OpenStreetMap.
items.brief: Growth along five rail "fingers" from the "palm" of the city, with green wedges kept open between them.

items.title: Curitiba BRT
items.designers: Jaime Lerner; IPPUC
items.scale: Citywide trunk network
items.placement: Placed at the city centre, approximate. Position from OpenStreetMap.
items.brief: Dedicated busways with tube stations and level boarding, set out together with land-use rules along structural axes.

items.title: Habitat 67
items.designers: Moshe Safdie
items.scale: 354 prefabricated modules
items.placement: Placed at the site. Position from OpenStreetMap.
items.brief: Stacked precast boxes give each apartment its own garden on the roof of the unit below: density with the qualities of a house.

items.title: Rotiers – Renovation of 46 housing units
items.designers: MULTIPLE Architecture & Urbanism; architecture team: FP architecture; structural engineering: GEI
items.scale: 3,916 m²; 46 housing units in a 1960s social housing building
items.placement: Placed at the city centre, approximate. Position from OpenStreetMap.
items.brief: Renovation of a 1960s social housing building that gives it a renewed identity while keeping the qualities of its wooded setting.

items.title: Novéo
items.site: Bassins à Flot mixed-use development zone (ZAC)
items.designers: Taillandier Architectes Associés (lead architect: Marinell Van Wyk; TAA Bordeaux); architecture office: Lanoire & Courrian
items.scale: 13,688 m²; 117 housing units (21 affordable homeownership, 37 social rental) in four buildings, a serviced residence and a 128-space shared car park
items.placement: Placed at the site. Position from OpenStreetMap.
items.brief: Four buildings combining 117 homes, a serviced residence and a shared car park in Bordeaux's Bassins à Flot district.

items.title: Hotel MS Collection Arouca
items.site: Former Monastery of Santa Maria de Arouca
items.designers: MiMool Arquitectura & Design de Interiores (lead architects: Fábio Milhazes, Rui Loureiro, Ana Ferreira, Joana Monteiro)
items.scale: 6,698 m²; part of a monastic complex classified as a National Monument since 1910, converted into a five-star hotel
items.placement: Placed at the site. Position from OpenStreetMap.
items.brief: Part of a monastery classified as a National Monument since 1910, rehabilitated as a five-star hotel.

items.title: Photography Studio as Local Infrastructure
items.designers: ArchTank (lead architect: Yasumasa Hayashi; architect: Nagi Kumagai); construction: Shinwa Kenko
items.scale: 269 m²; a flood-damaged neighbourhood photo studio rebuilt with a café, observatory and retail
items.placement: Placed at the city centre, approximate. Position from OpenStreetMap.
items.brief: A flood-damaged neighbourhood photo studio rebuilt as a small civic space with a café, observatory and shop.

items.title: Oxford Street pedestrianisation
items.site: Oxford Street, City of Westminster (first phase: Orchard Street to Great Portland Street)
items.designers: East (lead) with Gehl, Publica, J&L Gibbons, Etude and NRP; Hawkins\Brown (long-term vision for the whole street); overseen by the Oxford Street Development Corporation (Mayor of London)
items.scale: Almost 1 km traffic-free in the first phase, of a street about 2 km long; two new squares planned near Holles Street and Duke Street
items.placement: Placed at the site. Position from OpenStreetMap.
items.brief: Almost a kilometre of Oxford Street is now traffic-free, as a trial phase before the permanent scheme is built.

image.credit: Greater London Authority + Caroline Teo, via ArchDaily

items.title: Essen Central Library
items.designers: MVRDV with Meyer Architekten; interiors with Includi
items.scale: 11,000 m² across six storeys
items.placement: Placed at the site. Position from OpenStreetMap.
items.brief: A six-storey former department store turned into a city library designed as a public "living room".

items.title: Observatory, Landscapes of Waste
items.designers: Ryue Nishizawa (observatory); Kazuyo Sejima (supervision); Shingo Masuda + Katsuhisa Otsubo (plaza and bus stop); Suzuko Yamada (bus and visitor wear)
items.scale: Cone 33 m in diameter and 4 m high, overlooking a landfill basin
items.placement: Placed at the city centre, approximate. Position from OpenStreetMap.
items.brief: A 33-metre orange cone overlooking a landfill basin, built for the Setouchi Art and Industry 2026 festival.

links.label: Setouchi Art and Industry — festival website

image.credit: Setouchi Art and Industry, via Dezeen

items.title: Loco Park masterplan
items.designers: Stefano Boeri Architetti (founder Stefano Boeri; partner Pietro Chiodi)
items.scale: Not stated by the source
items.placement: Placed at the city centre, approximate. Position from OpenStreetMap.
items.brief: Competition-winning masterplan that renovates a locomotive factory and adds brick housing blocks, parks and public space.

items.title: Murphy Crossing MARTA infill station
items.site: Murphy Crossing, Southwest Atlanta (Adair Park, West End and Oakland City)
items.designers: Atlanta Beltline Inc. (preliminary scoping study; principal engineer Shaun Green)
items.scale: 20-acre Murphy Crossing site; 60-ft vertical gap between Beltline transit and MARTA rail; study costs about $800,000–$900,000
items.placement: Placed at the site. Position from OpenStreetMap.
items.brief: Five options for a new MARTA rail station that would give the Beltline its first direct connection to MARTA rail.

links.label: Atlanta Beltline — Murphy Crossing infill station virtual open house

image.credit: Atlanta Beltline Inc., via Urbanize Atlanta

items.title: Atlanta Beltline Northwest Trail – Segment 2A
items.site: Buckhead, from Bobby Jones Golf Course toward Peachtree Road
items.designers: Heath & Lineback (designers); PATH Foundation (program manager); Hasbun Construction (contractor); Atlanta Beltline Inc.
items.scale: 0.3-mile segment of 14-ft-wide multi-use trail, with a pedestrian bridge and an elevated trail structure; the full Northwest Trail will be 4.3 miles
items.placement: Placed at the site. Position from OpenStreetMap.
items.brief: A 0.3-mile trail segment with a pedestrian bridge and elevated section, linking the Beltline toward Peachtree Road job centres.

image.credit: Atlanta Beltline Inc., via Urbanize Atlanta

items.title: Grove Theatre revival
items.site: 1576 Donald Lee Hollowell Parkway NW, Grove Park
items.designers: Not named by the source; owner: Grove Park Foundation
items.scale: 10,400 sq ft of leasable space; $5.5 million renovation
items.placement: Placed at the site. Position from OpenStreetMap.
items.brief: A 1940s Westside movie house being renovated as a performing and cultural arts centre for Grove Park.

image.credit: Grove Park Foundation, via Urbanize Atlanta

items.title: GuildHouse
items.designers: Vida Companies (developer); Geheber Lewis Associates (architecture); Dix Hite (landscape); Krywicki (interior design); Kimley-Horn (civil engineering)
items.scale: 6.68 acres; about 310 apartments and 39 rental townhomes; 7,200 sq ft retail and coworking; $107.6 million; 15% workforce housing
items.placement: Placed at the site. Position from OpenStreetMap.
items.brief: About 310 apartments, 39 townhomes and retail planned on former industrial lots, with 15% workforce housing.

items.title: Jewel Streets Neighborhood Plan
items.site: Jewel Streets, East New York, Brooklyn and Lindenwood, Queens
items.designers: NYC Department of Housing Preservation and Development (HPD) with the Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) and the Mayor's Office of Climate & Environmental Justice; community partners: Justice for the Jewel Streets Coalition (East New York Community Land Trust) and Cypress Hills Local Development Corporation
items.scale: 12-block neighbourhood, including a 17-acre City-owned site; nearly $150 million in proposed infrastructure upgrades (per Urban Omnibus)
items.placement: Placed at the site. Position from OpenStreetMap.
items.brief: A City plan for a sunken, flood-prone 12-block neighbourhood: new drainage, rezoning, affordable housing and voluntary buyouts.

links.label: NYC HPD — Jewel Streets Neighborhood Plan
NYC HPD — Jewel Streets Neighborhood Plan (PDF)

items.title: Federal Boulevard BRT
items.designers: Not named by the source; funded by Colorado's Nonattainment Area Air Pollution Mitigation Enterprise
items.scale: Up to 18 miles and 74 stations; $50 million plus $2.7 million a year for maintenance
items.placement: Placed at one point on an 18-mile corridor. Position from OpenStreetMap.
items.brief: Bus rapid transit with 74 stations along up to 18 miles of one of metro Denver's busiest transit corridors.
